newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish MPs resign in boost to secularist Yilmaz.
newsitem.headline: Turkish MPs resign in boost to secularist Yilmaz.

text.p: Two Turkish MPs resigned from a pro-Islamic alliance on Friday, boosting an attempt by prime minister-designate Mesut Yilmaz to set up a secularist coalition.
Parliamentary officials said Islam-based Welfare Party deputy Ferit Bora had submitted a letter of resignation to the speaker's office.
The NTV television news channel said Bora would join a conservative splinter group that backs Yilmaz, the main opposition leader.
Anatolian news agency later said Erkan Kemaloglu, a member of the Islamists' conservative allies, had also quit. Kemaloglu was a deputy in Tansu Ciller's True Path Party.

Yilmaz has the backing of three other parties and President Suleyman Demirel but he still needs around half a dozen defections from the pro-Islamic alliance to win a vote of confidence in his planned coalition.
Secularist politicians were to begin drawing up the government programme and working out the distribution of ministries at talks later on Friday.
Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, the Welfare leader, resigned a week ago under pressure from the military. He plans to return to power in a coalition led by conservative Tansu Ciller.
